A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPDiffuser work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original MPDiffuser evaluations on D4RL, DSRL, custom control tasks, visual Pendulum, and Unitree Go2, together with experimental ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark, simulation, robot-deployment, and ablation results. Their retention from v2 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The planner and dynamics objectives, alternating sampler, ranking procedure, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. Appendix B newly specifies the existing ranker's architecture and training loss without reporting a modification to the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same D4RL/DSRL benchmarks, FetchPickAndPlace, Pendulum including visual observations, Car U-Maze, stochastic linear system, and Unitree Go2 tasks. Defective-joint adaptation and cross-dataset mismatch scenarios already appear in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark and ablation tables, including D-MPC, SafeDiffuser, planner-only controls, and combined-score sampling in their respective experiments. Newly cited physics-informed methods are discussed as related work rather than evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: The evaluation metrics, datasets and splits, sample budgets, training settings, and testing procedures are retained. The 100-versus-200-step control and combined-score weighting search in v3 Section 4.5 already appear in v2 Appendices H–I. Added ranker specifications are implementation disclosures.

E4.justification: v3 Section 4.5 relocates the denoising-budget control, alternation-versus-combination comparison, and distribution-mismatch analysis from v2 Appendices H, I, and L. Their questions and evidence are unchanged, as are the remaining conditioning, causality, noise-robustness, and sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains standard deviations and the same statement of five independent runs, each evaluated on 50 rollouts. No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing practice is added or revised elsewhere.

E6.justification: Matched tables, plotted results, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, visual Pendulum return remains -155.4 for MPDiffuser in Table 6, and mixed-dataset Hopper performance remains 70.3 in v2 Table 16 and v3 Table 10. Relocated analyses add no result entries.

T1.justification: The KL-constrained formulation, exponential-tilting derivation, score approximation, and operator-splitting rationale are retained, with v2 Appendix N becoming v3 Appendix K. Changing the CMDP tuple's cost-budget symbol from d to b corrects notation without changing the mathematical problem.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and concluding discussion retain the same claims about compositional sampling, dynamics consistency, safety, data efficiency, adaptation, and robot deployment. Moving supporting analyses into the main text does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly explains applicability when analytic system equations, differentiable simulators, or conservation laws are unavailable, and proposes integration with physics-informed learning. Existing result interpretations and the distribution-mismatch limitation are retained; the latter is simply moved into Section 4.5.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies a ranker MLP with two hidden layers of 64 units, trained using mean-squared error against rewards and costs. v3 also replaces the anonymous code-access link with a named GitHub link and adds a project-website link. These are documentation and access-information changes.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds a physics-informed-learning comparison citing PINNs, neural ODEs, Hamiltonian/Lagrangian networks, and Nath et al. The robot implementation gains attribution to Huang et al.'s locomotion work, while Reuss et al. (2023) is removed. This broadens context without substantially revising the central positioning.

P1.justification: Three existing appendix sections are consolidated into main-text Section 4.5, with corresponding roadmap and cross-reference updates. v3 also lightly edits the introduction, adds acknowledgements, and updates advising and conference information. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 Tables 12, 13, and 16 become main-text Tables 8–10 with column-width formatting. The Car U-Maze table moves closer to its experiment, and other floats and page breaks shift. Figure assets, plot designs, and table structures otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 fills a small reproducibility gap by documenting the ranker's architecture and loss in Appendix B. The added discussion clarifies its relationship to physics-informed approaches, while Section 4.5 makes existing controls and failure evidence more accessible. These changes modestly improve reproducibility and readability while preserving the work's scientific strengths and limitations.
